newsitem.title: GERMANY: BASF details special factors in results.
newsitem.headline: BASF details special factors in results.

text.p: German chemicals group BASF AG said on Wednesday that its 1996 pre-tax profit of 4.414 billion marks contained 517 million marks in net extraordinary factors.

The group spent 435 billion marks for restructuring and disinvestments, the group said in its annual report. Last year it sold its ailing BASF Magnetics unit to a Korean group and sold a portion of its stake in potash group Kali & Salz to a Canadian group.

Unforeseen writedowns totalled 266 million marks the group said, saying it needed to make adjustments for certain plants in Brazil and its stake in U.S. generics group IVAX, which has seen its share price plummet recently.
Some 302 million marks were spent on reserves for environmental matters while the group had special earnings of 486 million marks from insurance payments.
